paragraphs.text: The text presented here is not a gospel in the ordinary sense. It is a sayings source. The manuscript tradition calls it *The Damascus Codex*, though no Damascus has yet agreed to take responsibility for it.

What survives is not a life of Jack Feist, but a sequence of sayings, scenes, trials, fragments, and transmission-events surrounding the figure called Feist: a literary body, a pseudonymous teacher, a failed academic, a comic prophet, a wounded reader, a name too small for its work.
The old tradition says Q meant *Quelle*: source. This is Feist's source. Not the man behind the sayings. The sayings behind the man.

The full critical edition with apparatus by Rebekah Cranes is deposited at DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20752596. The entity resolution packet (EA-MPAI-FEISTSOURCE-01) is deposited at DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20752296.
